label: Calibrated observation recovers the endless population share from matching prefixes
paraphrase: The population mixes an endless share w in [0, 1] and a sourced share 1 − w with a fixed nonnegative normalized depth prior. At a cutoff k let t be the sourced matching-prefix probability and suppose the observed matching-prefix probability r factors as v times the latent mixture probability, for a common positive observation factor v ≤ 1. If t < 1, the share equals (r/v − t)/(1 − t). If t = 1, r equals v for every share. If t > 0, the ratio of endless to sourced observed matching-prefix probabilities is v/(v t) = 1/t. If the calibrated factor is positive at every length, r(k)/v(k) tends to w. Two such populations with the same observation profile and the same observed matching-prefix probabilities have the same endless share, even if their fixed proper sourced-depth priors differ.
